flashcards.q: What does AWS's own documentation say about relying on LocalStack for pre-production validation?
flashcards.a: Emulated features/APIs typically lag real service behavior, and tests passing locally can fail in the cloud due to IAM policy and quota interactions the emulator doesn't fully model. LocalStack is a dev accelerant, not a staging substitute.

flashcards.q: What changed about LocalStack's community vs pro Docker images as of the 2026.3.0 release?
flashcards.a: The two images were unified into a single image; service coverage is now gated by the entitlements tied to your auth token, not by which image you pulled. Free/Hobby tier still resets state on restart; persistent state (Cloud Pods) is a paid, Base-plan-and-above feature (~$45/mo).

flashcards.q: What does Ryuk do in Testcontainers, and where is it documented to fail?
flashcards.a: A sidecar container that removes all Testcontainers-labeled resources once the test-runner process exits, preventing leaked containers. Documented to fail on Docker-in-Docker and rootless-Docker CI configurations, leaking containers silently.

flashcards.q: What's the documented workaround for Ryuk failures on Docker-in-Docker CI runners?
flashcards.a: Set TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true for that runner, and add an explicit `docker container prune --filter "label=org.testcontainers=true"` cleanup step to the pipeline -- disabling Ryuk alone doesn't replace its cleanup function.

flashcards.q: Why does Testcontainers avoid the emulation-fidelity gap that LocalStack has to manage?
flashcards.a: It runs the actual dependency binary (real Postgres, Kafka, Redis) in a container for the test's duration instead of emulating its API -- there's no 'did the emulator model this correctly' question, at the cost of real container startup latency.

flashcards.q: What's the failure mode of an unpinned devcontainer base image?
flashcards.a: A mutable tag can be silently rebuilt upstream with different system package versions between when two engineers last rebuilt their container, so 'identical devcontainer config' doesn't guarantee an identical environment -- the same failure mode as an unpinned Docker production base image.

flashcards.q: At single-user scale, how does Ollama's token/sec throughput compare to vLLM's?
flashcards.a: Comparable -- both land in roughly the 130-180 tok/s band on the same hardware/model at single-user scale.

flashcards.q: Under concurrent load, what's the throughput and tail-latency gap between vLLM and Ollama, per published 2026 benchmarks?
flashcards.a: One benchmark: vLLM ~793 tok/s peak vs Ollama's 41 tok/s under the same concurrent load; P99 latency ~80ms for vLLM vs ~673ms for Ollama. The gap is architectural (vLLM's continuous batching + PagedAttention vs Ollama/llama.cpp's single-user design), not a tuning issue.

flashcards.q: What API compatibility does Ollama offer that makes it a low-friction local-dev substitute for a hosted LLM API?
flashcards.a: An OpenAI-compatible endpoint (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/models at localhost:11434/v1) -- code written against a hosted provider's API can point at Ollama with essentially a base-URL/API-key change.

flashcards.q: What problem do devcontainers solve, distinct from Testcontainers?
flashcards.a: Whole-team development environment parity (OS, runtime, tools, IDE config) as a versioned artifact -- not test-time dependency fidelity. Testcontainers spins up real dependency containers for a specific test's duration; devcontainers define what an engineer's environment looks like before any test runs.

flashcards.q: When should a test use LocalStack versus Testcontainers for the same class of AWS-adjacent dependency?
flashcards.a: Match the tool to what the test validates: SQL dialect/constraint fidelity (a real database) -> Testcontainers. 'Did the code call the right API shape' (e.g. S3 put_object) -> LocalStack is fine. Anything IAM- or quota-sensitive -> neither; use real staging AWS.

flashcards.q: Why is validating a RAG prototype's behavior against Ollama locally not sufficient evidence for production launch readiness?
flashcards.a: Ollama validation covers model behavior and prompt/response correctness, not concurrent-load throughput or tail latency -- the concurrency gap versus a production serving stack (vLLM) is architectural and invisible at single-user scale. A separate load test against the actual production serving stack is needed.
